questions.stem: What is the molecular formula of the compound with the condensed structural formula CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: Count the atoms: five carbons, eleven hydrogens on carbon plus one on the oxygen gives twelve, and one oxygen. Forgetting the hydrogen of the hydroxyl group gives C₅H₁₁O.

questions.stem: In a skeletal structural formula of an organic compound, what is shown at each corner and line end?
options: A hydrogen atom, with the carbon atoms implied by the lines between them
A carbon atom, but only when an oxygen or nitrogen atom is bonded to it
Any non-hydrogen atom, which must be identified from the molecular formula
A carbon atom, with enough hydrogen atoms implied to give it four bonds
questions.explanation: Skeletal formulae show carbon atoms as corners and line ends, with hydrogens on carbon left out. Atoms other than carbon and hydrogen, such as O in OH, are written in.

questions.stem: A skeletal formula is a zigzag of four carbon atoms with a double-bonded O on the second carbon. What is its molecular formula?
questions.explanation: The compound is butanone, CH₃COCH₂CH₃. Carbon 2 has no hydrogens, carbons 1 and 4 have three each and carbon 3 has two, giving C₄H₈O. C₄H₁₀O would be an alcohol with no C=O.

questions.stem: What is a condensation reaction?
options: A large molecule reacts with water and splits into two smaller molecules
A gas is cooled until it turns into a liquid without any change in formula
Two molecules join to form a larger molecule and a small molecule such as water
One molecule adds across a double bond with no other product being formed
questions.explanation: In a condensation reaction two organic molecules combine and a small molecule, often water, is released, as in forming an ester. Splitting a molecule with water is the reverse process, hydrolysis.

questions.stem: Butane, propanal, propan-1-ol and ethanoic acid have similar molar masses. What is their order of increasing boiling point?
questions.explanation: Butane has only dispersion forces; propanal adds dipole-dipole interactions; propan-1-ol forms hydrogen bonds; ethanoic acid forms more extensive hydrogen bonding through both its C=O and O-H. Similar size means the type of secondary interaction decides the order.

questions.stem: Why does ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH₂CH₂OH, have a much higher boiling point than propan-1-ol, although their molar masses are similar?
options: Its covalent O-H bonds are stronger and must break when the liquid boils
It is ionic in the liquid state, so strong ionic bonds must be overcome
It has two hydroxyl groups, so each molecule forms more hydrogen bonds
It has a longer carbon chain, so the dispersion forces between molecules are stronger
questions.explanation: Two OH groups per molecule allow more hydrogen bonding between molecules, so more energy is needed to separate them. Boiling does not break covalent bonds within molecules, and propan-1-ol actually has the longer chain.

questions.stem: Which compound is the least soluble in water?
questions.explanation: All four can hydrogen bond with water, but hexan-1-ol has a long non-polar hydrocarbon chain that disrupts the water's hydrogen bonding. Small molecules such as ethanol, propanone and ethanoic acid are miscible with water.

questions.stem: Iodine dissolves readily in hexane, poorly in water, and well in ethanol. Which explanation is best?
options: Iodine reacts with ethanol to form an ionic compound that is soluble in polar solvents such as water
Ethanol has a polar OH group and a non-polar ethyl group, so it can interact with both iodine and water
Ethanol is a non-polar solvent like hexane, so iodine dissolves equally well in both solvents
Iodine forms hydrogen bonds with ethanol molecules but cannot hydrogen bond with water molecules
questions.explanation: Non-polar iodine interacts with the hydrocarbon part of ethanol through dispersion forces, while the OH group lets ethanol mix with water. Iodine has no hydrogen bonded to N, O or F, so it cannot hydrogen bond.

questions.stem: Propanone is often used to clean grease from laboratory glassware and is then rinsed away with water. Which property makes it suitable?
options: It dissolves non-polar grease and is also miscible with water
It reacts with grease to form soap, which is then washed away
It is non-polar, so it repels water and dries the glass quickly
It forms strong hydrogen bonds between its own molecules only
questions.explanation: Propanone is a small polar molecule with non-polar methyl groups, so it dissolves many non-polar substances and also mixes completely with water. It does not saponify fats.

questions.stem: Which statement defines a secondary alcohol?
options: The carbon bearing the OH group is bonded to two other carbon atoms
The molecule contains exactly two hydroxyl groups on separate carbons
The OH group is on the second carbon atom of an unbranched chain only
The carbon bearing the OH group is bonded to one other carbon atom
questions.explanation: Alcohols are classified by the number of carbons attached to the carbon that carries the OH: one for primary, two for secondary, three for tertiary. A molecule with two OH groups is a diol, which is a different idea.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of (CH₃)₃COH?
questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the C-OH carbon has three carbons, with the OH and a methyl group both on carbon 2. It is a tertiary alcohol because that carbon is bonded to three other carbons.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: Number the three-carbon chain from the end nearer the OH: OH on carbon 1, methyl on carbon 2. Numbering from the other end would give the impossible 3-methylpropan-1-ol, which is really butan-1-ol.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of CH₃CH(OH)CH(CH₂CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain runs through the ethyl group, giving five carbons. Numbering from the end nearer the OH puts it on carbon 2 and a methyl group on carbon 3. Choosing a four-carbon chain gives 3-ethylbutan-2-ol, which misses the longest chain.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of HOCH₂CH(OH)CH₂OH, also called glycerol?
questions.explanation: Three OH groups on a three-carbon chain give the suffix -triol with locants 1,2,3, and the 'e' of propane is kept before a consonant. Propane-1,3-diol has only two OH groups.

questions.stem: Acidified potassium dichromate is warmed with a primary alcohol. What colour change is seen?
questions.explanation: Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to green Cr³⁺ as the alcohol is oxidised. Purple to colourless describes permanganate, and a silver deposit is the Tollens test.

questions.stem: Each alcohol is warmed with acidified dichromate. Which one leaves the solution orange?
questions.explanation: 2-methylbutan-2-ol is tertiary: the C-OH carbon has no hydrogen to lose, so it is not oxidised and the dichromate stays orange. The other three are primary or secondary and turn the solution green.

questions.stem: Butan-2-one is the oxidation product of which alcohol?
questions.explanation: Oxidising a secondary alcohol gives the ketone with the C=O on the same carbon. Butan-1-ol is primary and would give butanal and then butanoic acid; 2-methylpropan-2-ol is tertiary and is not oxidised.

questions.stem: Propan-1-ol is heated under reflux with excess acidified dichromate. What is the final organic product?
questions.explanation: A primary alcohol is first oxidised to the aldehyde, which under reflux with excess oxidant is oxidised further to the carboxylic acid. Propanone would come from the secondary alcohol propan-2-ol.

questions.stem: A student wants to collect propanal rather than propanoic acid from propan-1-ol and acidified dichromate. Which method is best?
options: Distil the aldehyde off as it forms, since it has a lower boiling point than the alcohol
Heat the mixture under reflux for a long time with a large excess of dichromate
Add the alcohol to concentrated sulfuric acid first, then add the dichromate
Use a tertiary alcohol instead, because it gives an aldehyde on mild oxidation
questions.explanation: Propanal has no hydrogen bonding between its molecules, so it boils below propan-1-ol and can be distilled out before it is oxidised further. Reflux with excess oxidant drives the reaction on to the acid.

questions.stem: Which half-equation shows the oxidation of ethanol to ethanal?
questions.explanation: Ethanol, C₂H₆O, loses two hydrogen atoms to become ethanal, C₂H₄O, released as 2H⁺ and 2e⁻. Electrons appear on the product side in an oxidation; the other equations are unbalanced or show reduction.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO?
questions.explanation: The CHO group is at the end of a four-carbon chain, so the name is butanal. The CHO carbon is counted in the chain, so it is not propanal.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of CH₃COCH(CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: The main chain has four carbons with the C=O on carbon 2 and a methyl on carbon 3, numbering so that the carbonyl gets the lowest locant. 2-methylbutan-3-one numbers from the wrong end.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CHO?
questions.explanation: The aldehyde carbon is always carbon 1. Counting from the CHO end, the methyl branch is on carbon 3 of a four-carbon chain, giving 3-methylbutanal.

questions.stem: Which compound is a ketone?
questions.explanation: A ketone has a C=O group bonded to two carbon atoms, as in pentan-3-one. CHO is an aldehyde, COO between two carbons is an ester, and COOH is a carboxylic acid.

questions.stem: Ethanal is warmed with Tollens reagent, and a silver mirror forms on the inside of the test tube. What happened to the ethanal?
options: It was reduced, forming ethanol as the silver ions were oxidised
It was oxidised, forming propanone in the alkaline solution
It was hydrolysed, forming methanal and methanoic acid in solution
It was oxidised, forming ethanoate ions in the alkaline solution
questions.explanation: Tollens reagent is alkaline, so the oxidised aldehyde is present as the carboxylate ion, CH₃COO⁻. The silver ions gain electrons and are reduced to silver metal, forming the mirror.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds can be distinguished by warming with Tollens reagent?
questions.explanation: Tollens reagent is reduced to a silver mirror by aldehydes but not by ketones, so pentanal gives a mirror and pentan-2-one does not. In each of the other pairs, both compounds give the same result with Tollens reagent, so they cannot be told apart.

questions.stem: Why are aldehydes readily oxidised while ketones are not?
options: The aldehyde carbonyl carbon carries a hydrogen atom; the ketone carbonyl carbon does not
The aldehyde has a C=C double bond next to its carbonyl group; the ketone does not
Ketones are already carboxylic acids, so they cannot be oxidised any further
The ketone carbonyl group is at the end of the chain, where it is protected from attack
questions.explanation: Oxidation of an aldehyde replaces the H on the carbonyl carbon with OH, giving a carboxylic acid. A ketone's carbonyl carbon is bonded to two carbons, so oxidation would require breaking a C-C bond.

questions.stem: An unknown compound C₄H₈O turns warm acidified dichromate from orange to green. Which compound could it be?
questions.explanation: Butanal and butanone both have the formula C₄H₈O, but only the aldehyde is oxidised by dichromate. 2-methylpropan-2-ol is C₄H₁₀O and tertiary, and butanoic acid is C₄H₈O₂ and cannot be oxidised further.

questions.stem: Butanal is oxidised once with acidified dichromate and once with Tollens reagent. What are the organic products?
options: Butanone in acid conditions; butanoic acid in the alkaline Tollens reagent
Butan-1-ol in acid conditions; butanoate ions in the alkaline Tollens reagent
Butanoic acid in acid conditions; butanoate ions in the alkaline Tollens reagent
Butanoate ions in acid conditions; butanoic acid in the alkaline Tollens reagent
questions.explanation: The same oxidation occurs in both, but in alkaline solution the carboxylic acid is deprotonated to its carboxylate ion. Butan-1-ol would be a reduction product, and butanone cannot form from a straight-chain aldehyde by oxidation.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of HOOCCOOH?
questions.explanation: Two carboxyl carbons make a two-carbon chain with a COOH at each end, so the name is ethanedioic acid. Both carboxyl carbons count in the chain.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂COOH?
questions.explanation: The carboxyl carbon is carbon 1 of a four-carbon chain, and the methyl branch is on carbon 3. Numbering from the other end is not allowed because the COOH carbon must be carbon 1.

questions.stem: Why is ethanoic acid described as a weak acid?
options: It contains only one hydrogen atom in each molecule
It does not react with metal carbonates or hydroxides
Only a small proportion of its molecules ionise in water
Its solutions always have a low concentration of solute
questions.explanation: Strength describes the extent of ionisation: CH₃COOH + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H₃O⁺ lies well to the left. Concentration is a separate idea, and ethanoic acid has four hydrogen atoms, only one of which is acidic.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium hydrogencarbonate solution?
questions.explanation: An acid and a hydrogencarbonate give a salt, water and carbon dioxide, so effervescence is seen. Sodium ethanoate is CH₃COONa because Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ combine one to one.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the reaction of propanoic acid with sodium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Carbonate accepts two protons, so two acid molecules react with one Na₂CO₃ to give two sodium propanoate, water and carbon dioxide. Carbonic acid is not written as a product because it breaks down to water and carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: 6.00 g of ethanoic acid reacts with excess sodium hydrogencarbonate. Use H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0. What mass of sodium ethanoate, CH₃COONa, forms?
questions.explanation: n(CH₃COOH) = 6.00 / 60.0 = 0.100 mol, and the ratio is 1 : 1, so n(CH₃COONa) = 0.100 mol. Its molar mass is 82.0 g mol⁻¹, giving 8.20 g. Assuming 2 : 1, as with carbonate, gives 4.10 g.

questions.stem: Solid hexanoic acid is barely soluble in water, but dissolves when sodium hydroxide solution is added. Why?
options: It forms hexan-1-ol, which can hydrogen bond with water more effectively
It forms sodium hexanoate, whose ions form strong ion-dipole interactions with water
Sodium hydroxide shortens the hydrocarbon chain, making the molecules more polar
Sodium hydroxide raises the temperature, which always increases solubility
questions.explanation: The acid is deprotonated to hexanoate ions. Ion-dipole interactions between charged ions and water are much stronger than the hydrogen bonds the neutral acid can form, so the salt is far more soluble.

questions.stem: A household cleaner containing ethanoic acid removes white calcium carbonate scale from taps. Which observation and explanation fit?
options: Bubbles form as the scale is converted to soluble calcium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide
Bubbles form as the scale is converted to insoluble calcium ethanoate and hydrogen gas
No bubbles form because ethanoic acid is too weak an acid to react with any carbonate
No bubbles form because the scale simply dissolves in the water of the cleaner
questions.explanation: 2CH₃COOH + CaCO₃ → Ca(CH₃COO)₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Weak acids still react completely with carbonates as the reaction removes the ions, and hydrogen gas comes from acids with active metals, not carbonates.

questions.stem: Which compound is the most soluble in water?
questions.explanation: Potassium pentanoate is ionic, and its ions are strongly hydrated by water through ion-dipole interactions. The other three are neutral molecules of the same size whose five-carbon chains limit their solubility.
